description: Transform the globe into a full-viewport interactive interface. Remove scroll-driven camera. Add drag-to-rotate interaction, cinematic landing fly-in, floating glass cards at species locations (positioned via Three.js world-to-screen projection), and geospatial layer toggle UI. The globe IS the app after the landing sequence.
steps: STEP 1 - Rewrite index.html: Remove the entire scroll-container, overlay-container, landing-sequence layers, and Barba wrapper. Replace with: (a) canvas#cinematic-canvas (full viewport, fixed), (b) a div#globe-ui-container for globe overlays (layer toggle pills, floating species cards container, back button), (c) a minimal loading screen, (d) a div#safari-container (hidden by default, used for species deep-dive). Keep the noscript fallback. Remove the old nav, progress bar, habitat-anim divs, species-grid, numbers-grid, vision section entirely.

STEP 2 - Rewrite src/main.js: Remove Lenis, ScrollTrigger, Barba.js, OverlayUI, hover-3d imports and usage. The new main.js should: (a) Init CinematicEngine, (b) Init Globe with interactive mode (drag-to-rotate via pointer events), (c) Run a cinematic landing sequence (camera flies from far space to Earth over 3s using GSAP timeline, not scroll), (d) After landing completes, show the globe UI (layer toggles, floating cards), (e) Set up card click handler that triggers immersive zoom transition into safari scene, (f) Set up 'return to globe' handler. Remove all scroll-driven logic.

STEP 3 - Rewrite src/cinematic-engine.js: Remove CAMERA_KEYFRAMES and interpolateKeyframes (scroll-driven). Keep: Three.js scene, camera, renderer, EffectComposer with bloom, particle system, lighting, resize, animation loop with onUpdate callbacks. Add: (a) A method flyCamera(fromPos, toPos, fromTarget, toTarget, duration, ease) that returns a GSAP timeline for camera transitions, (b) A method setCameraPosition(pos, target) for immediate placement, (c) Store initial camera position for 'globe view' state. Change scene background to dark (0x0a0a1a or similar deep space color) to match the space-to-Earth cinematic feel.

STEP 4 - Rewrite src/globe.js: Keep: sphere geometry, Earth texture, atmosphere shader, HOTSPOTS array, latLngToVector3, species data loading, layer system (columns, habitat discs, protected areas). Remove: auto-rotation (user controls rotation now). Add: (a) Drag-to-rotate via pointer events (mousedown/mousemove/mouseup on canvas - rotate group.rotation.y and group.rotation.x with inertia), (b) A method getScreenPositions(camera) that projects each unique species hotspot position to 2D screen coords (using vector.project(camera) then converting to CSS pixels), returning array of {species, screenX, screenY, scale, visible} where visible=false if facing away from camera (dot product check with camera direction), (c) A method getSpeciesPosition(slug) returning the 3D world position for a species (average of its hotspots), (d) Expose speciesDataCache for card rendering.

STEP 5 - Create src/floating-cards.js: This module renders floating glass cards as HTML elements positioned over the globe. (a) On each frame (called from main.js render loop), get screen positions from Globe.getScreenPositions(camera), (b) For each unique species, position a div.floating-card at that screen location using position:fixed; transform:translate(), (c) Cards that are facing away (visible=false) get opacity:0 with transition, (d) Cards scale based on z-depth (closer = larger), (e) Each card shows: species name, IUCN status badge, and a small thumbnail from the first photo in species data, (f) Cards have frosted-glass styling (backdrop-filter: blur, semi-transparent white bg, border-radius, subtle border), (g) Cards are clickable - clicking triggers the immersive zoom callback passed during init, (h) Support toggling card visibility based on active layer (only show when species layer is active).

STEP 6 - Update src/style.css: Remove all scroll-container, overlay, landing-sequence, site-nav, habitat-anim, numbers-grid, species-grid, vision styles. Add: (a) .floating-card styles (frosted glass: background rgba(255,255,255,0.15), backdrop-filter blur(20px), border 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.2), border-radius 16px, padding, box-shadow, transition for opacity/transform, pointer-events auto, cursor pointer), (b) .floating-card__name, .floating-card__status badge styles, (c) .floating-card__thumb (small circular image), (d) .layer-toggle-bar styles (fixed bottom center, flex row of pill buttons with glass effect), (e) .layer-toggle-btn styles (active state with accent color), (f) #globe-ui-container as fixed overlay container, (g) Dark body/html background (#0a0a1a) to match space theme, (h) Loading screen styles (centered, minimal), (i) .return-to-globe button styles (fixed, glass-style, top-left corner when in safari mode).

STEP 7 - Remove src/overlay-ui.js (no longer needed - scroll overlays are gone). Remove src/hover-3d.js (cards no longer have scroll-based 3D hover). Update or remove src/transitions.js to only export what the new main.js needs (the zoom-into-safari transition logic). Delete the files that are fully replaced.

STEP 8 - Update vite.config.js: The species/*.html pages will still exist as separate entry points for SEO/fallback, but the primary experience is now the single-page globe interface. Keep the multi-page input config as-is for backwards compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build succeeds without errors
index.html contains no scroll-container or overlay sections - it has canvas, globe-ui-container, and safari-container
main.js does not import Lenis, ScrollTrigger, OverlayUI, or hover-3d
CinematicEngine has flyCamera method and dark background
Globe supports drag-to-rotate and exposes getScreenPositions and getSpeciesPosition methods
floating-cards.js exists and renders positioned HTML cards from globe data
style.css has .floating-card glass styles and dark background theme
Layer toggle UI (species/habitat/threats) is rendered in index.html
verification: Run `npm run build` in /projects/sandbox/species-on-screen and confirm exit code 0 and dist/ output
